maturity_contract: H0-Candidate; H1-Source-reviewed; H2-Buildable; H3-Platform-integrated; H4-Operationally-qualified for a named profile; H5-Deployment-authorized for a named customer/environment. Reference and gap entries cannot be treated as products.

items.name: OpenWrt One hardware (board revision must be pinned)
items.named_model_or_revision: OpenWrt One 1; exact board revision and production lot not yet pinned
items.observed_evidence: The OpenWrt Techdata record identifies the model as OpenWrt One 1, says it is available in 2026 and lists current upstream support release 25.12.5, the MediaTek MT7981BA, 1 GB RAM, NAND/flash, 2.5 GbE WAN and 1 GbE LAN. Official design pages expose KiCad schematic files and board/schematic PDFs. These upstream facts do not prove vetted South African stock, exact batch condition, complete BOM/license audit, or deployment suitability.
open_blockers: Pin exact purchased board revision and supplier lot.
Review licenses for each design artifact and verify a complete BOM and substitutions.
Validate firmware trust/update/recovery, radio configuration, VLAN/firewall throughput and fail-safe behavior.
Test availability, lifecycle support and physical-unit behavior.

items.name: OCP Meta Minipack3 network switch design package v1.0
items.observed_evidence: OCP lists a Minipack3 design package in its networking design-file catalogue; no specific build vendor, fully audited source revision, or purchasable configured unit is selected here.
open_blockers: Pin the exact design package and revision; identify applicable hardware/IP license terms.
Review schematics, layout, BOM, firmware, CPLD/boot and manufacturing package completeness.
Identify manufacturer/assembler, exact supported NOS image and lifecycle support.
Qualify management-plane isolation, port compatibility, thermals, acoustics, power and failure recovery.

items.name: Open Compute Project server design ecosystem (no exact server SKU selected)
items.observed_evidence: OCP publishes multiple server specifications and design files. This entry is an ecosystem/source-of-design pointer, not a qualified platform or ordered BOM.
open_blockers: Choose exact design and production supplier appropriate to small-site and datacenter needs.
Audit exact source files, license, BOM, firmware and management controller.
Verify serviceability, supply-chain traceability, spares, warranty, noise, power and thermals.

items.name: Open Compute Project storage designs (no exact storage SKU selected)
items.observed_evidence: OCP lists storage chassis/sleds, device and technology specifications; the catalogue does not select a complete drive/controller/system configuration.
open_blockers: Select exact chassis, controller, drives and firmware revisions.
Define encryption/key custody, secure erase, integrity checks, backup/restore and replacement policy.
Measure performance, endurance, failure recovery and local sourcing/lead time.

items.name: Open Compute Project Rack & Power design ecosystem
items.observed_evidence: OCP covers rack systems and rack-level power conversion, storage and control; it is a standards/design resource, not a selected UPS or PDU.
open_blockers: Select compatible 19-inch rack, PDU, UPS/battery and power distribution configuration.
Qualify local electrical compliance, surge/brownout response, battery replacement, alerting and runtime sizing.
Document rack loads, grounding, thermal envelope and maintenance.

items.name: BeagleV-Fire RISC-V/FPGA development board
items.observed_evidence: Official docs link hardware design files and schematics. Suitable for lab, interface, trusted-boot and edge-acceleration research, not assumed to be a production server or certified security module.
open_blockers: Pin board/FPGA bitstream and toolchain revisions and review licenses.
Check Linux/NixOS support, boot chain, FPGA image update and recovery.
Assess industrial temperature, long-term supply and real workload/peripheral support.

items.name: OpenTitan Earl Grey production silicon and open design ecosystem
items.named_model_or_revision: Earl Grey v1.0.0 production silicon top-level; commercial part/package not yet identified
items.observed_evidence: Official OpenTitan documentation states that Earl Grey production silicon is in production and release v1.0.0 is the first production silicon; the project timeline records fabrication beginning with Nuvoton in February 2025 and the first production deployment in Chromebooks in March 2026. Luminous has not selected a purchasable part/package/module or verified its supply, integration fit, certificate scope, or deployment suitability.
open_blockers: Identify the concrete Nuvoton part number, package and ordering channel; verify supply and lifecycle for the target region.
Review exact RTL/release and silicon stepping, datasheet, errata, validation evidence, product security advisories and license terms.
Establish how keys are provisioned and protected, the trust/attestation interface, secure recovery, and whether the proposed module fits the target host.
Keep upstream chip production status separate from Luminous integration qualification and any customer certification/authorization.

items.name: Framework Laptop 13 documentation and modular hardware family
items.observed_evidence: The upstream repository publishes CAD, module documentation, connector pinouts and partial mainboard documentation under CC BY 4.0. It does not publish a complete public mainboard schematic set; NixOS lists Framework among devices with official hardware-team testing.
open_blockers: Choose an exact mainboard generation, SKU, Wi-Fi module and firmware baseline.
Pin source revision and audit license scope and all proprietary firmware dependencies.
Qualify secure boot/TPM, suspend, docking, fleet deployment, firmware update, spares and lifecycle.
Keep endpoint authorization separate from NixOS compatibility.

items.name: MNT Reform open-hardware laptop family (model selection required)
items.observed_evidence: MNT publishes design files for open hardware; the official shop explicitly marks the Reform v0 listing as an older version no longer sold.
open_blockers: Identify a currently supported model and source repository; do not base procurement on Reform v0.
Pin parts and licenses, check component availability, firmware and NixOS compatibility.
Qualify performance, repair logistics, service support, identity hardware and lifecycle before workforce use.

items.name: LibreRouter board design (historical lead; successor review required)
items.observed_evidence: The GitHub hardware repository is archived and states that development moved to GitLab. No current successor revision or manufacturing availability has been qualified.
open_blockers: Inspect the successor repository and identify a maintained exact hardware revision.
Confirm open license, native file completeness, BOM and manufacturability.
Validate radio compliance, firmware support, secure update, parts sourcing and operational maintenance.

items.name: OpenBMC out-of-band management firmware (software integration reference)
items.observed_evidence: OpenBMC is a source-available management-controller distribution with a supported-machine list; upstream states supported-machine functionality/maturity varies and is not warranted.
open_blockers: Select a specific server/BMC combination explicitly listed and supported by the vendor.
Review source revision, vendor extensions, signing, network exposure, credentials and update/recovery controls.
Disable or isolate unnecessary management interfaces; validate separate OOB network and access logging.

items.name: coreboot firmware compatibility (model-specific integration reference)
items.observed_evidence: coreboot supports a model-specific range of platforms; firmware support does not imply that all required vendor silicon initialization, microcode or peripheral firmware is open.
open_blockers: Choose an exact mainboard and verify current board-status, maturity and any binary blobs.
Qualify measured boot, TPM integration, update recovery, IOMMU and peripheral initialization.
Do not promise fully open firmware without a per-component binary audit.

items.name: Validated cryptographic module / HSM (exact product not selected)
items.observed_evidence: NIST maintains the authoritative CMVP database for FIPS 140 module validation. The register intentionally names no module because validation scope/status and customer requirements must be matched to exact module, firmware and use.
open_blockers: Define jurisdiction, threat model, key custody, interface and performance needs.
Select exact module/certificate and verify active status, certificate scope, firmware version, operational environment and allowed mode.
Choose a separate non-US procurement/assurance route where required; a certificate does not authorize the full network.

items.name: Managed campus switch, PoE and Wi-Fi access point (exact SKUs not selected)
items.observed_evidence: Open network operating systems and open switch design projects exist, but the portfolio has no chosen switch/AP SKU with verified chipset support, RF approvals, lifecycle and supplier stock.
open_blockers: Select supported managed L2/L3/PoE switch and AP models with exact hardware revisions.
Verify 802.1X/RADIUS, VLAN enforcement, WPA3-Enterprise where required, roaming, logging, firmware support and factory reset behavior.
Document radio certification and country-specific channel/power rules; qualify wired management path.

items.name: Production server and managed endpoint SKUs (not yet selected)
items.observed_evidence: Design ecosystems and Linux compatibility references are available, but no production server, workstation or endpoint bill of materials has been selected for Luminous support.
open_blockers: Set workload, form factor, RAM/ECC, CPU, NIC, TPM, GPU and serviceability floors.
Select at least one supportable server and endpoint configuration, including exact motherboard and firmware variants.
Collect vendor lifecycle, warranty, spare availability, BOM, origin/provenance and firmware update disclosures.

items.name: Production storage, backup target and removable recovery media (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: OCP provides storage specifications and reference designs, but Luminous has not selected exact drives, controllers, chassis or backup media.
open_blockers: Select drive/SSD models and firmware based on endurance, power-loss protection, endurance and availability.
Define immutable/offline backup tiers, encryption keys, restore objectives, sanitization and media retirement.
Run restore and failure tests against the exact storage/software revision.

items.name: NICs, optical transceivers, fibre/copper cabling and link budget (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: Interoperability specifications exist, but exact NICs, optics, switches, cable lengths and validated module combinations are not chosen for any supported deployment profile.
open_blockers: Set throughput, port count, reach, redundancy and oversubscription targets per reference deployment.
Verify compatibility matrix, firmware/driver support, optical budgets, supplier authenticity and replacements.
Test error counters, failover, heat and link recovery using physical interfaces.

items.name: UPS, PDU, environmental and rack monitoring (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: Open infrastructure and manageability specifications provide reference material, but no local-market UPS/PDU/sensor models or monitoring protocols have been verified.
open_blockers: Measure real load and define target runtime, battery aging and graceful shutdown behavior.
Select serviceable models with status protocol/API, replacement batteries and local support.
Test mains loss, brownouts, battery degradation alerts, sensor failure and network isolation.

items.name: Identity tokens, smart cards, readers and provisioning station (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: Identity token and key-management hardware has not been selected; appropriate assurance and identity proofing requirements depend on each relying party and jurisdiction.
open_blockers: Specify credential protocol, lifecycle, key generation, revocation, recovery and account recovery threats.
Select exact tokens/readers with relevant validation/certifications and supported enrollment software.
Keep identity-proofing, crypto-module validation and whole-system approval claims distinct.

items.name: Independent out-of-band console and recovery access (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: OOB management design practices and firmware projects exist, but there is no selected isolated console server, management switch, BMC configuration or offline recovery kit.
open_blockers: Define dedicated management plane and local break-glass access without depending on production LAN/WAN.
Select hardware and validate MFA, source addressing, credential rotation, audit, firmware trust and reset behavior.
Test that losing central services or normal network access does not prevent safe recovery.

items.name: Approved voice/video collaboration endpoints (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: No voice/video endpoint, SBC, handset, codec or conferencing appliance is selected. Procurement and information-handling requirements vary widely by environment.
open_blockers: Choose collaboration threat model, encryption and meeting identity requirements.
Select supported client devices and gateway/handset SKUs; review update support, microphones/cameras and telemetry.
Do not imply certified secure voice or classified use without product- and deployment-specific authorization.

items.name: WAN/ISP handoff, cellular backup and remote-site antenna hardware (not selected)
items.observed_evidence: Remote-site connectivity cannot be finalized until fibre/ISP, LTE/5G backup, antenna, SIM/eSIM, carrier and regulatory requirements are defined for target regions.
open_blockers: Define uptime target and acceptable provider/carrier dependencies.
Select exact modem/router/antenna SKUs supported by software, approved for operating country and available locally.
Test failover, bandwidth caps, power loss, carrier loss, remote recovery and SIM/key handling.

items.name: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 Update 1 supply-chain risk management reference
items.observed_evidence: NIST describes multi-level cyber supply-chain risk practices and the current page notes the November 2024 update; use it as a risk-management reference, not as product certification.
open_blockers: Map relevant controls to each deployment profile and procurement contract.
Maintain supplier, component provenance, vulnerability, obsolescence and exception evidence.
Use other jurisdictional requirements where NIST is not the applicable authority.

items.name: Framework Laptop 13 AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series (exact configuration still to qualify)
items.named_model_or_revision: Framework Laptop 13 AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series; exact RAM, wireless module, board revision and firmware not selected
items.observed_evidence: The official Framework Linux compatibility page lists the Ryzen AI 300 Series model and lists NixOS as community-supported, with Wi-Fi/Bluetooth working out of the box but fingerprint-reader setup required; support differs by generation/configuration. These are vendor compatibility notes, not a Luminous NixOS image or endpoint security qualification.
open_blockers: Verify current South African ordering, import, warranty, repair and spare-part support; do not infer local stock from the vendor product page.
Choose exact mainboard generation, RAM, wireless module and firmware baseline and pin the deployable configuration.
Qualify secure boot/TPM, firmware update and rollback, IOMMU, sleep/resume, docking, device enrollment and recovery for the intended NixOS profile.
Check lifecycle/support terms, firmware/proprietary binary dependencies, hardware revision changes and replacement-unit reproducibility.

items.name: South African DPSA public-service ICT/security policy index (applicability review required)
items.observed_evidence: The official DPSA standards index lists public-service information-security directive material (2022), a Public Service ICT Security Assessment Standard and checklist (2018), ICT Security Guidelines and service-continuity guidance (2017), MIOS v6, and older policy items including FOSS policy and MISS. The index alone does not establish current applicability to a particular agency, contract or information class.
open_blockers: Retrieve and review the actual signed directive, circulars and current agency ICT/security policies; confirm whether each older standard remains applicable or has been superseded.
Map each applicable requirement to product controls, evidence, procurement clauses, data classification and acceptance tests.
Confirm with the contracting authority whether additional sector-specific, critical-infrastructure, privacy, cryptographic or cross-border requirements apply.

items.name: SITA public-sector ICT hardware and security procurement routes (contract applicability must be checked)
items.observed_evidence: SITA's effective-panel page says listed contracts are available to public bodies, parastatals and organs of state; as viewed 2026-10-10 it lists the information-security products/services panel RFA 2494-2021 ending 2027-09-06 and the server-room/network-cabling related panel RFA 2168-2024 ending 2031-10-10. It also lists UC/VC panel RFA 2501-2021 ending 2026-10-08, which is past the snapshot date and is not treated as current. SITA's hardware page lists RFB 2009 (2026-04-20 to 2027-04-20) and RFB 740 (2025-11-24 to 2026-11-24); actual scope, amendments and category fit must be confirmed against the tender/contract documents. The SITA tender administration listing also showed RFB 3261-2026 for Ethernet switches, wireless LAN, WAN routers, backhaul, copper/fibre cabling and related services with a closing date of 28 August 2026; that date has passed as of this snapshot, so it is historical market evidence rather than an open opportunity.
open_blockers: Read actual engagement models, technical specifications, terms, accredited-supplier lists and amendments; the public landing page alone is not tender qualification.

Determine whether Luminous should be a product vendor, open-source software supplier, subcontractor, integration partner or supplier through an accredited reseller; none is assumed eligible by this record.
Confirm current contract validity, commodity coverage, licensing terms and procuring authority instructions immediately before any bid or quote.
Prepare commercial support, warranty, SLA, security evidence and local delivery obligations that open-source publication alone does not provide.
Treat tenders whose published closing date has passed as historical only; monitor new calls and verify amendments on the official tender portal.
